segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I wanted to walk through the revised order form for 42 seats, the calibration module, and the two-hour admin training. Target start date is May 6, with go-live June 3.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That lines up. My main thing is invoice timing. Finance asked if the annual invoice can be dated May 1, net 30, so it lands in the right month.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, May 1 and net 30 are both in the order form. Total is $38,640 for the year after the standard 6% volume tier on 40-plus seats. No separate services fee for the training.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. And if we add, say, 8 more seats in July, is that prorated or a new line item?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Prorated through the same term, ending April 30 next year. It would be the same per-seat rate, billed when you add them. Pretty straightforward.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. Legal had one question on the auto-renewal language. We need 60 days notice instead of 30. Is that something you can put in?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, 60 days is within our standard terms. I’ll send the updated version after this call, and it’ll show the notice period right on page 3.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. For implementation, our plant managers can only attend training Wednesdays after 1 Eastern. Does your team have June 5 open?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: They do. I’ve got June 5 at 2 Eastern held for the admin session, and the kickoff on May 8 at 11. I’ll include your ops lead, Marcus, and our implementation lead on the calendar invites.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Send me the updated order form and I’ll route it for signature today. Assuming no surprises, you should have it back by Friday.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Sounds good. I’ll send it in the next half hour with the May 1 invoice date, 60-day renewal notice, 42 seats, and June 3 go-live called out.
